name: CRR_USAbdomen_Adult_Indicators
title: US Abdomen - Adult: referral indicators
publisher: Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora - Community Referred Radiology Programme
description: Atomic clinical indicators for the US Abdomen (Adult) national referral criteria (National Community Referral Criteria for Imaging Part I, v2.0, published 09/04/2026, pp.30-33). DEMO TRANSCRIPTION - NOT CLINICALLY REVIEWED. The LLM extraction step, structured referral forms and the Criteria Viewer tick-list all produce a QuestionnaireResponse against this Questionnaire, which the CQL library CRR_USAbdomen_Adult evaluates. Each answer may carry the answer-evidence extension (status documented|inferred, quote). No item carries an initialExpression: there is no population library for this site.

National red-flag indicator used in this site's logic
Painful jaundice

extension.valueString: Answer false (documented) when the note says the jaundice is painless.

item.text: Unintentional weight loss
Unintentional, unexplained weight loss
Liver blood tests and other laboratory results
ALP as a multiple of the upper limit of normal reported by the laboratory

extension.valueString: The ALP result at the initial presentation, as a multiple of the laboratory's upper limit of normal. Omit when the note gives a value without a stated multiple or flag.

item.text: Alkaline phosphatase high
GGT raised (higher than the upper limit of normal)
GGT as a multiple of the upper limit of normal reported by the laboratory

extension.valueString: The initial GGT result as a multiple of the laboratory's upper limit of normal.

item.text: Liver blood tests have been repeated 3 months or more after the initial presentation
ALP remains higher than the upper limit of normal on repeat testing
GGT remains higher than the upper limit of normal on repeat testing
GGT on repeat testing as a multiple of the upper limit of normal reported by the laboratory
The raised liver blood test result is isolated (the other liver blood tests are normal)
Bilirubin raised
ALT value (IU/L)
Ferritin raised
Previous imaging
Biliary tree has previously been imaged
The presenting problem has previously been imaged

extension.valueString: true = the presenting problem has been imaged before.

item.text: Previous imaging has shown gallstones
Assessment
An obvious cause for the jaundice has been identified

extension.valueString: true = an obvious cause for the jaundice is stated; false = the note says there is no obvious cause.

item.text: The patient is a potential candidate for and would accept a cholecystectomy
Conservative methods (e.g. weight loss and lifestyle alterations or medication change) have been unsuccessful
Clinical features of concern are present

extension.valueString: true = features of concern are present; false = the note says there are none.
